phases.note: TWO INHERITED ITEMS. (1) BRANCH A CONFIRMED by phase 2's probe 2026-09-06, so error_code='dispatched' is now a HISTORICAL value carried only by rows written before phase 2 landed. Keep NINA_JOB_STAGE_LABEL.dispatched and jobStage's dispatched branch -- they are not dead code, those rows are the first thing on /nina/jobs -- but do not present it as a live stage; only the copy's tense changes. (2) FROM PHASE 6 (landed b4bc490), with a correction the coordinator verified: 14 nina_turns image jobs have an args.replyToId resolving to nothing, reported by nina:memory-reap and never deleted (invariant 9), so planJobJump's 'gone' arm and its NINA_JOB_JUMP_NOTE copy are LIVE on real rows -- build and test them as the common case. But REJECT phase 6's advice to treat 'the triggering message is gone' and 'the session was removed' as ONE state: it proved the converse of what that needs. The cascade means no message survives a deleted session; collapsing the states requires that no message is GONE while its session SURVIVES, and deleteNinaMessage does exactly that -- unchanged by phase 6 (per lib/db/schema.ts:857, which phase 6 itself wrote) and reachable in production from lib/admin/chatPhotoActions.ts:231 and :283. Collapsing them would tell a runner 'the session was removed' about a job whose session is alive and whose message they deleted through /admin. Keep the kinds distinct. Phase 6 also withdrew its 'larger than the plan guessed' framing: 14 dangling replyToIds vs the plan's 15 error_code='dispatched' rows are different predicates, possibly non-overlapping. Not a scope increase.
